title: Regular Taylor jet matrices and frozen-rank minor ideals
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $R$ a commutative ring, $\sigma$ a finite variable index set, $c:k[x_j]_{j\in\sigma}	o R$ a ring homomorphism, and $D_j:R	o R$ derivations, represented as $\mathbf Z$-derivations [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For a multi-index $
u\in\mathbf N^\sigma$, define $
u!=\prod_j
u_j!$ and $D^
u$ by iterating $D_j$ in the finite index order. Reuse the exponent, factorial and finite-minor constructions of [def-trf-formal-taylor-jet-matrices]. For $t\ge0$, let $E_t=\{\gamma:|\gamma|\le t\}$. Given $h_1,\ldots,h_s\in R$, the regular jet matrix [def-weil-matrix] has rows $E_t$, columns $\{1,\ldots,s\}	imes E_t$, and entry $0$ when $\eta
ot\le\gamma$, otherwise $c(1/(\gamma-\eta)! )D^{\gamma-\eta}h_i$, where the scalar is first inverted in $k$. For any finite matrix, its $r$-minor ideal is the ideal [def-trf-minor-ideal] after reindexing rows and columns by finite ordinals. For a homomorphism $e:R	o L$ to a field, define the frozen-rank jet minor ideal to be the ideal of the $(\operatorname{rank}_L(e(P_t(h)))+1)$-minors [def-weil-matrix-rank] of $P_t(h)$. These definitions include the empty family, empty variable set, zero ranks and oversized minors. In characteristic zero and for commuting coordinate derivations, the iterates and factorial inverses have the usual Taylor meaning.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Remarks 9.1, 9.5, pp.265--268,275--277; explicit regular matrices in lem-trf-regular-taylor-minor-equality-germ. Definition ownership extraction required by H2 return of 73da211d444b.
